headline: Unicorns multiply. Funding flows. Delays persist.
deck: This week, private space valuations rise while delays in hypersonic testing continue.

stories.head: True Anomaly raises $190M, eyes co-orbital security
stories.body: True Anomaly secured a $190 million Series C round, pushing its valuation to $1.6 billion. This funding will bolster its co-orbital security and space domain awareness capabilities, a timely move given the rising geopolitical tensions in space. The Department of Defense's increasing interest in these technologies suggests that True Anomaly is well-positioned to capitalize on government contracts.
stories.soWhat: When a company raises this much, it’s a sign that the defense sector is finally taking space security seriously.

stories.head: Katalyst Space joins the unicorn club with $12M
stories.body: Katalyst Space has raised $12 million for a GEO servicing demo mission, marking its entry into the unicorn ranks. This funding aims to develop capabilities for satellite repairs and servicing, a niche that is increasingly essential as the number of satellites in orbit grows. With this capital, Katalyst is positioning itself as a key player in the satellite maintenance market.
stories.soWhat: Who knew fixing satellites could be a billion-dollar business? Just wait until they start charging for 'space insurance.'

stories.head: Hypersonic glide-vehicle test postponed again
stories.body: The hypersonic glide-vehicle test has slipped for the third consecutive quarter, raising concerns about the viability of these systems. Delays like this not only impact timelines but also funding and strategic planning for defense contractors involved in hypersonic technology. The ongoing setbacks suggest that the U.S. may be lagging behind its competitors in this critical area.
stories.soWhat: If this keeps up, 'hypersonic' might just become a euphemism for 'we're still figuring it out.'

watchlist.title: Keep an eye on Anduril and L3Harris
watchlist.body: Their collaboration on a tactical SDA constellation bid could set the tone for future defense contracts.

watchlist.title: Watch for SpaceX's secondary market activity
watchlist.body: With SpaceX's valuation at $470 billion, any movement could signal investor confidence or caution.

watchlist.title: Monitor the FY27 budget developments
watchlist.body: The additional $1.4 billion for space resilience could lead to new contracts for emerging players.

watchlist.title: Expect updates from PiLogic and the Air Force
watchlist.body: Their partnership on satellite fault-prediction software could yield important insights for the satellite industry.

talent.statLabel: Job orders YoY · plus 2 starters per head, an 8-year first
talent.head: Demand has doubled. So has our hit rate.
talent.body: EVONA's job orders are up 2.0× year-over-year, and for the first time in our eight-year history we're placing two new starters per EVONA staff member. The first number says demand is real. The second says we're converting it, which in recruitment is the only number that actually matters. Growth is heaviest in Series B/C startups; primes are running flat. Compensation isn't the variable. The constraint is schedule risk in the primes: senior engineers leave Boeing, Lockheed, Northrop because they want to ship hardware before retirement.
